metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >45), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model underreacts; increase forecast slightly to reflect sentiment shift.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is negative; add 2–5% bias to first 5 days.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 50+ peak), model holds too high; apply exponential decay correction (e.g., 0.95 multiplier per day).
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent history; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
- For events with official announcements (e.g., policy changes, auction results), model often lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast up by 2–5% for next 2–3 days.
